title: Matheseos Libri VIII, Vol. 1 (Latin)
author: Julius Firmicus Maternus
description: Matheseos Libri VIII, Volume 1, by Julius Firmicus Maternus, in the Latin critical edition by Wilhelm Kroll and Franz Skutsch (Leipzig: Teubner, 1897), containing Books I-IV and the preface to Book V. Written around 334-337 CE by a Sicilian rhetorician who later converted to Christianity, the Mathesis is the longest and most complete surviving Latin manual of astrology. Book I defends astrology against its critics and argues that the stars signify rather than compel human fate. Following books explain the signs, planets, houses, aspects, decans and lots, and give hundreds of interpretations of planetary positions in the nativity, drawing on Hellenistic sources attributed to Nechepso, Petosiris, Hermes and Abraham. It preserves the famous 'Thema Mundi', the horoscope of the world's birth. It is a key source for Hellenistic astrology and Hermetic cosmology in the Latin West.
